params.formula: C = S_0 e^(-qT) N(d_1) - K e^(-rT) N(d_2); d_1 = (ln(S_0/K) + (r - q + 1/2 sigma^2) T)/(sigma sqrt T); d_2 = d_1 - sigma sqrt T; vega = S_0 e^(-qT) phi(d_1) sqrt T (2.10)

solver.method: Newton on sigma with the analytic vega, the bracket [lo, hi] narrowed by the sign of the price error, a bisection step whenever Newton would leave it or vega is zero; stop when |price error| <= price_tol x max(1, |price|) or the bracket is narrower than sigma_tol
solver.bounds: max(S_0 e^(-qT) - K e^(-rT), 0) <= C <= S_0 e^(-qT) (call); max(K e^(-rT) - S_0 e^(-qT), 0) <= P <= K e^(-rT) (put) -- a price outside has no implied vol and is refused

symmetric.model: S_T = f_j F e^(-1/2 sigma_j^2 T + sigma_j sqrt T Z) with probability p_j; Sum p_j f_j = 1 keeps E^Q[S_T] = F; price = Sum p_j C_BS(f_j S_0, K, r, sigma_j, T)

skewed.why: the high-vol component carries the lower forward: down-moves come with high vol, the market's skew in miniature; 0.75 x 1.05 + 0.25 x 0.85 = 1

hedging.fee_note: 10 basis points of the value of every share traded, at setup, at each rebalance and at the unwind
hedging.drift: mu = r for every path set (Decision -- owner may overrule): under the pricing drift the discounted stock is a martingale, so E[hedged P&L] = E^Q[e^(-rT) payoff] - P_0 = 0 for every N and every hedge (2.8), and the spread carries the whole story; 2.7 showed the hedge is drift-blind in the limit
